messages.subject: LGCP optimization problem
parts:
Hello,

I am working on a model of sardine preferentially sampled data. I have followed the chapter 4 of the spde book and I have run a LGCP (Gamma-Poisson) model.

I have fitted a model with not shared smoothed bathymetry ("rw2) and another with just shared spatial effect and the results seem to be ok. However, when I run a model including the covariate (bathymetry) and the spatial effect the next error appears repeatedly:

file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: 0bed76828f01  date: Tue Sep 03 11:21:49 2019 +0300
Function: GMRFLib_build_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 758, Thread: 0
Variable evaluates to NAN or INF. idx=(2399,2399). I will try to fix it...

I saw on a post from some years ago that someone already had this problem and Haakon Bakka suggested it would need good priors to fix it. I have used pc.priors with a logic value for the range and I think it works fine when I look at the model hyperparameters output.

Despite of this, when I include the covariate the mentioned error appears and also the the corrected sd values are not good (eigenValues also quite  high):

Compute corrected stdev for theta[0]: negative 0.624263  positive 1.000000
Compute corrected stdev for theta[1]: negative 1.091022  positive 1.000000
Compute corrected stdev for theta[2]: negative 1.000000  positive 0.549892
Compute corrected stdev for theta[3]: negative 1.000000  positive 0.582806
Compute corrected stdev for theta[4]: negative 1.431875  positive 1.000000
Compute corrected stdev for theta[5]: negative 1.000000  positive 13.000841

I attach the code with some plots and the model result just in case it helps. I have also tried setting a prior for the covariate getting better values of the precision parameter but I must be missing something else.  If someone has a suggestion about what is happening or how could I improve the optimization process I would be very grateful.

Thanks in advance,

Fran

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] LGCP optimization problem
parts:
file: smtp-taucs.c hgid: 0bed76828f01 date: Tue Sep 03 11:21:49
> 2019 +0300
> Function: GMRFLib_build_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 758, Thread: 0
> Variable evaluates to NAN or INF. idx=(2399,2399). I will try to fix
> it...
>

simply says that something (like the linear predictor) creates an
overflow (most likely), so something goes towards +/- infinity.
althrough there are steps taken to try to prevent this, it might not be
successful as in the case here.

Also

Compute corrected stdev for theta[0]: negative 0.624263 positive
1.000000
Compute corrected stdev for theta[1]: negative 1.091022 positive
1.000000

...


shows a bad sign, the corrections should in general be, one just below
1, and the other one, just above 1. if exactly eq to 1, its a bad sign
in the case that the estimate was to weird and it revert back to 1.

this mean that there is no good corresponance between the computed
Hessian and output of the correction procedure. It usually means, that
the mean is not accuractely enough located, which again might be due to
the problem above.

All of this, in most cases, are due to a to flexible model with not to
much information in the data. The data is what they are, so you may try
to tighten the model up with more informative priors to see what
happen.

If the problems comes because of an added covariate, then check that
the covariate is properly scaled, like x=scale(x), and set a very
informative prior for that coefficient. If 'x' confound to much with
the spde, you can constrain the spde to be orthogonal to that one, but
personally, I find this approach to be somewhat questionable.

Best
H
